transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining me to review the eighth-grade civics oral-history project before I make my approval decision. I'd like to start by hearing from each of you about the draft plan — particularly your thoughts on the proposal to use personal phones for audio recording, publish all recordings on the public school website, and retain the files indefinitely. I want to make sure we've thoroughly considered the implications before moving forward.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. I'm glad we're reviewing this carefully. Before we get into the recording and publication questions, I need to raise an important issue about the student roster. My project roster review shows that only eight of the proposed twenty student interviewers have actually completed the district's media-ethics training, which is required before any student can conduct recorded interviews. We'll need to address that gap and make sure the approval file includes proper training-verification records before moving forward.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, from my technology review, I need to flag several critical issues with the draft plan's recording and storage approach. Personal phones cannot be used for school recordings — the project must use district tablets instead. All files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive, not on personal devices or general storage. Additionally, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation — indefinite retention is not permitted. Finally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record documenting these safeguards before approval can proceed.

Thank you all for these critical findings. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I make my decision:

First, from Ms. Patel: only 8 of the 20 proposed student interviewers have completed the required media-ethics training. That means only those 8 are currently eligible to conduct recorded interviews.

Second, from Mr. Lewis: interviewees I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 have not granted permission for public web publication — their recordings must be excluded from the public website and limited to internal archive use only.

Third, from Ms. Romero: personal phones cannot be used — district tablets are required. Files must go in the restricted OralHistory drive, not general storage. Indefinite retention is not permitted — recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation. And a secure-storage configuration record must be documented.

Before I settle on my approval decision, I want to confirm: Ms. Patel, can you provide me with the specific IDs of the 8 students who have completed the media-ethics training? I'll need those to finalize the approved interviewer list. And to all three of you — are there any additional concerns beyond what you've raised today that I should be aware of?
